newsitem.title: USA: Odwalla says has completed juice recall.
newsitem.headline: Odwalla says has completed juice recall.

text.p: Odwalla Inc said it has completed the voluntary recall of its apple juice and other apple juice-based products that health authorities have associated with an outbreak of bacterial disease.

The number of people health authorities said were confirmed or suspected to be suffering from the E. coli infection in three western states and British Columbia has risen to 66, with most of these linked to drinking of apple juice.
Odwalla, which had announced the voluntary recall after its products were linked to the outbreak at mid-week, said its apple-related products had been removed from 4,600 outlets.

Odwalla distributes its fresh fruit juices in seven western states and in British Columbia and the company said sale and distribution of its citrus-based juices and geothermal water were continuing in the region.

Odwalla said the company and government health authorities are testing its fresh apple juice and juices which contain apple juice "to determine whether they could have played a part in recently-identified cases of E. coli O157:H7..."

The company noted the relation between its apple juice products and E. coli O157:H7 infection at the moment remains epidemiological, based on the linkage between people who have been infected by E. coli and who have consumed the product.

The E. coli microbe, which is potentially fatal to humans, lives within the intestines of cattle and can spread to humans via fecal contamination of food. It can cause sometimes bloody diarrhea, stomach cramps and a slight fever.

Odwalla said consumers who have purchased any of the 16 the Odwalla products it has recalled should destroy or return the products for a full refund, and the company set up a toll-free telephone number to answer consumer questions. The number is 800 639-2552.
